text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Privatisation Commission will soon hire financial advisers through competitive bidding for the privatisation of Pakistan International Airlines.

- The performance of private investment in the first three years of the Eighth Five Year Plan was not encouraging as the actual investment of 439.8 billion rupees (1992/93 prices) was only 46.4 percent of the Plan target of 948.4 billion.
- The caretaker government is contemplating major changes in the existing structure of the civil bureaucracy, apparently to improve its efficiency and avoid inter-service rivalries.
- There was an almost total breakdown in inter-city telephone communications on Tuesday following damage to an optic fibre cable in Multan.

- Karachi business centres, wholesale markets and shops remained closed on Tuesday in response to the strike called by Sipah-i-Sahaba against the killing of its chief Zia-ur-Rahman Faruqi and others in the Lahore bomb blast on Saturday.
- The Federal Government has promulgated three ordinances to amend the Bank Nationalisation Act 1974, Banking Companies Ordinance 1962 and State Bank of Pakistan Act 1956.
- The government has invited foreign and local investors to develop hotels, motels, theme parks and tourist resorts.
- The government plans to review drugs prices to control increases.
- Habib Bank Ltd has ordered its branches to show real profit.
